<center>
*The theory, science and practice of designing and deploying socio-technically responsible machine learning systems.*
</center>

<br>

<div class="row">
  <div class="col" markdown="1">

  **Instructor**: [Lucas Rosenblatt](https://lucasrosenblatt.com/). Please call me Lucas.

  **Class Times**: Mondays and Thursdays, 1:10-2:25pm in [ROOM].

  **Office Hours**: In **TCL 308**. Open drop-in on Wednesdays, 1:30-2:30pm. Appointment blocks Mondays 4:00-5:00pm and Thursdays 2:30-3:30pm; see the [syllabus](syllabus.html) for how to book.

  **Communication**: [Piazza]([PIAZZA_URL]) for content questions; [Slack]([SLACK_CHANNEL_URL]) for casual discussion and team coordination. Please try to use these channels before emailing me; see the [syllabus](syllabus.html) for which to use when.

  </div>
  <div class="col" markdown="1">

  **Labs**: Mondays, 2:30-4:00pm in [LAB_ROOM]. Alternating problem weeks and presentation weeks. See the [Labs](labs.html) page.

  **Quizzes**: Short quizzes on Mondays covering the prior week's lectures or a recent homework. 10 total, 1 point each and additive, and you start with 1 point banked, so you can miss one and still earn full credit.

  **Exams**: Midterm in class on Thu Oct 15. We will vote to decide whether the final is in the December exam period or in the last lecture block on Thu Dec 10.

  **Project**: Semester-long project in groups of two. See the [Project](project.html) page.

  </div>
</div>

**Some Potentially Useful Resources**: [Fairness and Machine Learning](https://fairmlbook.org/) | [CS 860: Algorithms for Private Data Analysis](https://www.gautamkamath.com/CS860-fa2020.html) | [Review of Probability Theory](https://cs229.stanford.edu/section/cs229-prob.pdf)
